subject: Banking
title: The Equifax Data Breach
description: A quick win: understand The Equifax Data Breach.

hook.text: In 2017, Equifax was hacked. Personal data of 147 million Americans was stolen, including Social Security numbers.

buildup.text: Hackers exploited a known software flaw that Equifax failed to patch for two months.

discovery.text: Names, addresses, Social Security numbers, and credit card numbers were exposed.

twist.text: Equifax executives sold $1.8 million in stock before the breach was announced. They knew before the public did.

climax.text: The company that holds America's most sensitive data couldn't protect it.

punchline.text: 147 million records stolen. Executives sold stock first. The company survived.

quiz.question: How many Americans were affected by the Equifax breach?

details.summary: The 2017 Equifax data breach exposed Social Security numbers, birth dates, and addresses of 147 million Americans, roughly half the US adult population, in one of the most consequential cybersecurity failures in history.
details.whyItMatters: The Equifax breach demonstrated that the companies holding our most sensitive financial data are not adequately protecting it. Stolen Social Security numbers enable identity theft indefinitely because unlike a password, you cannot change your SSN.
takeaways: 147 million Americans had personal data exposed in the 2017 breach
Equifax failed to patch a known software vulnerability for months
The company paid 700 million dollars in settlements but no executive faced criminal charges

faq.question: How did the Equifax breach happen?
faq.answer: Hackers exploited a known vulnerability in Apache Struts software that Equifax failed to patch for over two months despite a fix being available. Once inside, attackers exfiltrated data for 76 days before Equifax detected the intrusion.

faq.question: What can victims of the Equifax breach do now?
faq.answer: Place credit freezes at all three bureaus, monitor credit reports regularly, and use the free credit monitoring that Equifax was required to provide. Since SSNs cannot be changed, vigilance must be maintained indefinitely.
